news.headline: SBP likely to keep interest rate unchanged at 11.5% at July 27 MPC meeting, survey shows
news.summary: Published Jul 21, 2026: a Topline Securities survey found 97% of market participants expect the State Bank of Pakistan's Monetary Policy Committee to hold the policy rate at 11.5% when it meets July 27, 2026 (only 3% expect a 100bps cut), citing heightened geopolitical uncertainty and the recent rebound in international oil prices despite contained inflation; the SBP last reviewed policy on June 15, 2026, also holding at 11.5%. About 49% of respondents expect the rate to remain at 11.5% by December 2026 while 46% foresee further easing; Topline Research itself expects the rate to fall below 11.5% by year-end. This is a market-expectation survey ahead of the decision, not the decision itself - logged as impact 3 (notable/guidance) pending the actual MPC outcome on July 27.

news.headline: Pakistan seeks $10 billion US exchange stabilisation facility to bolster forex reserves
news.summary: Reported Jul 21-22, 2026 (Reuters exclusive, citing a source): Pakistan has formally requested a $10 billion bilateral exchange stabilization facility from the US Treasury (addressed to US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent), with a maturity of up to five years, aimed at strengthening forex reserves, supporting the rupee and reducing reliance on multilateral lenders; the request followed Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb's meeting with Bessent in Washington on Tuesday (Jul 21). Pakistan remains under its existing $7 billion IMF programme. Not yet approved/finalised by the US side per sources reviewed - logged as impact 3 (relevant, moderate) pending confirmation of any agreement.

news.headline: Brent crude tops $92/bbl, nearly six-week high, as Houthis threaten Saudi Red Sea blockade and US strikes Iran for 10th straight day
news.summary: Published Jul 22, 2026: Brent crude trading at $92.71/bbl (TradingEconomics), up 1.87% on the day and its highest level in nearly six weeks; separate wire figures cited Brent above $92/bbl generally. Drivers: the US carried out a 10th consecutive day of strikes against Iran after President Trump vowed Tehran 'will pay' for attacks that killed American soldiers, and separately dismissed the likelihood of imminent US-Iran talks while warning of further strikes; a Kuwaiti-flagged tanker carrying oil products was struck near the Strait of Hormuz; Yemen's Houthi militants threatened to blockade Saudi Arabia's maritime traffic in the Red Sea, emailing shipowners advising against calling at Saudi ports, with at least three tankers already reported to have U-turned in the southern Red Sea; the US pledged retaliation if the Houthis disrupt Red Sea shipping; Saudi Arabia is rerouting crude via pipelines to cut reliance on the Strait of Hormuz; separately, attacks on the Caspian Pipeline Consortium terminal on Russia's Black Sea coast are disrupting Kazakhstan's crude exports. Sharp, multi-corridor commodity/supply-risk move per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10) - direct read-through for Pakistan's OMC (PSO), refiners (ATRL, NRL, PRL), E&P names (MARI, OGDC, PPL), gas utilities (SNGP, SSGC) and HUBC, plus renewed inflation/import-bill and current-account pressure economy-wide; escalation flagged.

news.headline: UBL profit rises 33% in H1 2026 as deposits hit record Rs6.1 trillion
news.summary: Following UBL's 262nd board meeting (Jul 22, 2026): consolidated H1 2026 profit after tax Rs85.9bn (EPS Rs34.3), up 33% YoY; Q2 2026 alone profit after tax Rs37.5bn (EPS Rs14.97), up 31% YoY but down 23% QoQ; deposits hit a record Rs6.1trn, up 43% YoY and 13% QoQ; H1 non-interest income Rs73.8bn (+123% YoY); H1 net interest income Rs189.7bn (+8% YoY); Q2 operating expenses Rs48.4bn (+35% YoY, +19% QoQ); Q2 cost-to-income ratio 40% vs 33% in Q2 2025; effective tax rate 52%. PSX/DPS company page confirms a 'Financial Results for the Quarter ended 30 June 2026' filing was submitted Jul 22, 2026; no interim dividend per-share figure for this quarter was disclosed in the sources reviewed (UBL's April 15, 2026 board meeting had separately declared a Rs8/share interim dividend for Q1, already outside this newslog's coverage window) - logged as impact 4 (material earnings result, core-tier stock at ~8% index weight) pending confirmation of any new dividend rate in a follow-up cycle.

news.headline: S&P upgrades Pakistan's sovereign credit rating to 'B' from 'B-', first 'B' rating in nine years
news.summary: Published Jul 22, 2026, corroborated by ProPakistani ('S&P Global Upgrades Pakistan's Credit Rating After 9 Years') and Express Tribune ('S&P upgrades Pakistan's credit rating to 'B' from 'B-', highest level in eight years'): S&P Global Ratings raised Pakistan's long-term foreign- and local-currency sovereign rating to 'B' from 'B-', with a stable outlook, and separately upgraded the transfer-and-convertibility assessment to 'B' from 'B-'; short-term rating affirmed at 'B'. S&P cited 'stronger institutional capacity, sustained implementation of International Monetary Fund (IMF)-backed reforms, improved fiscal performance, and a significant rebuilding of foreign exchange reserves,' noting foreign exchange reserves rose to $25.3bn (end-June 2026) from $6.7bn (December 2022), tax revenues rose 3.2 percentage points of GDP in the year to June 2025, and it projects the general government fiscal deficit at 4% of GDP in FY2027 versus nearly 8% in FY2022-23; S&P projects GDP growth of 3.5% in FY2027 after 3.6% in FY2026. S&P cautioned Pakistan's interest burden remains among the highest for rated sovereigns and that weakening fiscal discipline or external deterioration could prompt a downgrade. A sovereign rating upgrade is a market-wide policy/macro event per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10) - logged as impact 5 and flagged for escalation.

news.headline: Pakistan invites Samsung to make country a smartphone export hub
news.summary: Published Jul 22, 2026: Federal Minister Jam Kamal Khan encouraged Samsung to 'look beyond Pakistan's domestic market and export Pakistan-manufactured smartphones to emerging markets, particularly Africa,' and endorsed establishing certified mobile-phone refurbishment facilities in Pakistan; government committed to examining taxation concerns 'within the broader fiscal framework' and linking incentives to investment, localisation, exports and value addition. Samsung's delegation flagged that changes in the taxation structure and a narrowing tariff differential between Semi Knocked Down (SKD) and Completely Built Unit (CBU) categories had reduced the competitiveness of locally manufactured phones, requesting maintained tariff protection. No investment figures, export targets, or PSX-listed company named directly in the article; tagged to AIRLINK as the universe's listed smartphone/electronics assembler for sector-relevance context, not a direct company mention.
